levels.title: Ignore the Deletes
levels.story: Rowan gives Kit a magic rule for the afternoon: nothing Kit does can undo anything. Kit steps onto the Bridge and finds that the Cabin is still there too. "Handy," says Kit. "Can I plan like this?"

everyday.scene: When you imagine tidying a room without ever having to put anything away, you guess how long it will take much faster. The guess is rough, but it takes no effort.
everyday.question: How can a planner estimate the work left without solving the whole problem?
everyday.answer: It solves an easier copy of the problem in which no action undoes a fact, and uses the length of that plan as its guess.

lessons.title: A world without deletes
text: Delete relaxation makes an easier copy of the problem by ignoring every delete list. Once a fact is true, it stays true. In the relaxed world Kit can stand at the Cabin and the Bridge at once, and keep a parcel while it also lies where it was.

text.text: Delete relaxation keeps every action's preconditions and add effects, and drops only the delete effects. So any real plan still works in the relaxed world, and a shortest relaxed plan is never longer than a shortest real plan.

terms.meaning: A simpler copy of a problem that is easier to solve.
A plan that works when delete lists are ignored.

lessons.title: Layer by layer
text: Start with the facts true now. In each round, add every fact that an applicable action would add, and keep all the earlier facts. Stop when every goal fact has appeared. In Kit's world that takes 4 rounds.
Tracing back from the goals shows which actions were needed. Here a relaxed plan has 6 actions: pick p, two moves, drop p at the Dock, pick q, and drop q at the Cabin.

lessons.title: Cheap but not exact
text: The length of a relaxed plan makes a guess for the search. In Kit's world it says 6 at the start, while the real shortest plan needs 8. The relaxed Kit never has to walk back, because Kit at the Cabin is never deleted.
Finding the very shortest relaxed plan is itself hard (NP-hard), so planners such as FF build a good relaxed plan quickly instead of the best one.

deeper.title: A guess that can be high

text.text: Because FF's relaxed plan is not guaranteed to be the shortest one, its length is not guaranteed to be an admissible guess, and can sometimes be above the true cost. The perfectly shortest relaxed plan would make an admissible guess.

fieldNotes.title: FF heuristic
fieldNotes.text: The FF planner searches forward and uses a heuristic that estimates goal distance by ignoring delete lists.

fieldNotes.title: FF at the competition
fieldNotes.text: FF was the most successful automatic planner at the AIPS-2000 planning competition.

fieldNotes.title: Cost of the best guess
fieldNotes.text: Computing the exact length of an optimal relaxed solution, which would make an admissible heuristic, is NP-hard.

summary: You ignored delete lists to make an easier problem, grew the facts round by round, traced back a relaxed plan of 6 actions, and saw why that guess is usually below the real 8.
Rowan tips an imaginary hat. "The magic wore off at dusk." Kit grins. "But the guess it gave me was good enough to start with."

mistake.title: Treating a relaxed plan as a real plan
mistake.text: A relaxed plan can use facts that the real world would have deleted, like standing at the Cabin after leaving it. It is only a guess, not something Kit can follow.
